newsitem.title: FRANCE: FIRS maintains French 97/98 sugar crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: FIRS maintains French 97/98 sugar crop estimate.

text.p: French sugar intervention board FIRS said on Monday that it did not release a new forecast this month for the national 1997/98 beet sugar crop because there was no significant news to justify an adjustment.
In its first forecast for the new 1997/98 season issued in mid-April FIRS predicted that France may produce 4.20 million tonnes of beet sugar against 4.226 million in 1996/97.
The estimate assumed sowings would slightly ease to 420,000 hectares from 422,000 hectares and sugar yield reach 10.0 tonnes per hectare from 10.01 tonnes in 1996/97.
FIRS said at the time there were worries about a possible impact of a persisting drought on crops but that the estimate did not reflect these fears.

"We did not issue a new forecast because basically there was nothing new. There were drought concerns but then the rain came," a FIRS official told Reuters, following the release of the FIRS report for May.
Asked if this meant FIRS was maintaining its April forecast, the official said "yes".
Last week French planters said rain since the last week of April helped accelerate beet growth and that crop prospects should further improve if a combination of rain and warm temperatures held.
